# WhisprCatch, in full

Last updated: 2026-08-15. Everything below is checkable against the source at
https://github.com/AviroopPaul/whisper-catch (MIT licence).

## One paragraph

WhisprCatch is a free, open-source push-to-talk dictation app for macOS and Linux. You hold
a key, speak, and let go; punctuated, capitalised text is typed into whatever application
has focus. Speech recognition happens on your own CPU, so nothing is uploaded, there is no
account, and there is no subscription. It is frequently searched for as an open-source or
free alternative to Wispr Flow.

## How it works

1. Hold the push-to-talk key. Right Command on macOS, Right Alt on Linux, both
   reconfigurable to keys such as Left Command, Right Control, Super, F13 or Scroll Lock.
   A small floating pill appears to show the app is listening.
2. Speak normally. You never say "period" or "new paragraph"; punctuation and capitalisation
   come from the model. The microphone keeps a 300 ms pre-roll so the first syllable is not
   clipped when you start talking immediately after pressing the key.
3. Release. The transcription is typed at the cursor. With streaming enabled (the default)
   words appear live while you are still speaking, and the remainder lands on release.

## Privacy and networking

- Inference runs locally as int8 ONNX through ONNX Runtime, using the transcribe-rs crate.
- There are zero network calls during dictation.
- Audio is decoded in memory and never written to disk.
- The app contains no analytics, telemetry or crash reporting of any kind.
- The only network access is a one-time model download during first-run setup. After that
  the app works with networking disabled.
- Transcription history, if enabled, is stored locally in history.jsonl and can be turned
  off or cleared from settings.

## Models

- NVIDIA Parakeet 0.6B: about 660 MB, the more accurate option, default on Linux.
- Moonshine base: about 64 MB, small and quick, default on macOS.
- Both run int8 on the CPU at roughly 25 times realtime. No GPU is used or required.
- The model can be switched at any time in settings.

## Platforms

- macOS 11 or newer, Apple Silicon only. Installed via Homebrew cask:
  `brew install --cask AviroopPaul/whisprcatch/whisprcatch`
- Ubuntu and Debian, x86-64, via a .deb package: `sudo apt install ./whisper-catch_amd64.deb`
  Works on X11 and Wayland. Keyboard access needs one polkit prompt.
- Any other platform can build from source with `cargo build --release -p whisper-catch`.
- Not supported: Windows, iOS, Android, Intel Macs.

## macOS permissions, in order

WhisprCatch needs Accessibility, Input Monitoring and Microphone access. The first-run
wizard opens each System Settings pane. macOS only re-reads permission grants when an
application starts, so the app must be quit and reopened once after granting them. Running
`whisper-catch doctor` prints which grants are live and which model is loaded.

Release builds are signed with a stable self-signed certificate rather than ad-hoc, because
macOS keys those three permission grants to an app's designated requirement. Homebrew is
the supported install path; the cask clears the quarantine flag after verifying the
download's SHA-256.

## Configuration

Config lives at `~/Library/Application Support/whisper-catch/config.toml` on macOS and
`~/.config/whisper-catch/config.toml` on Linux. Options include the push-to-talk key, the
model, live streaming on or off, the recording overlay, and local history.

## Cost comparison

WhisprCatch costs $0 and has no paid tier, so there is nothing to upgrade to and no usage
cap. For context, paid cloud dictation apps generally charge between $8 and $25 a month.
Wispr Flow, the best-known of them, lists Pro at $12 a month billed annually or $15
month-to-month (wisprflow.ai/pricing, checked August 2026), which is $144 to $180 a year and
roughly $432 to $540 over three years.

## What WhisprCatch deliberately does not do

- No AI rewriting of tone or style. It types what you said.
- No cloud sync between devices.
- No learned personal dictionary or custom vocabulary yet.
- No snippets or text expansion.
- No mobile apps.
- No team accounts, admin console or central billing.

If any of those matter to you, a paid cloud tool is genuinely the better choice. The
comparison page at https://whisper-catch.vercel.app/wispr-flow-alternative/ lays out both
sides row by row.

## Frequently asked

**Is there a free, open-source alternative to Wispr Flow?** Yes, WhisprCatch. Same
hold-to-talk gesture, runs locally, costs nothing, MIT-licensed, and unlike Wispr Flow it
has a native Linux build.

**Does my voice leave my computer?** No. The model runs on your CPU; nothing is uploaded.

**Do I need a GPU or internet?** Neither, apart from the initial model download.

**How accurate is it?** For straightforward dictation it is close to paid cloud tools.
Cloud tools do better on personalised vocabulary and multilingual switching.

**Is it really free?** Yes. There is no paid tier in existence.

  models, tray, plus the whisper-catch CLI binary.
